hints: Differentiate each parametric coordinate with respect to $\theta$ first.
When differentiating the double-angle terms, include the factor $2$ from the chain rule.
Form the curve gradient by dividing $dy/d\theta$ by $dx/d\theta$.
Keep the numerator and denominator grouped so their signs and terms remain clear.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the parametric equations with respect to $\theta$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\theta}(2\sin\theta + \sin 2\theta) = 2\cos\theta + 2\cos 2\theta$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\theta}(2\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta) = -2\sin\theta - 2\sin 2\theta$$

hints: For a vertical tangent, solve $dx/d\theta=0$ and later confirm $dy/d\theta$ is not zero.
Convert the double-angle cosine in this equation into a quadratic expression in $\cos\theta$.
Solve the quadratic and use $0<\theta<\pi$ to discard inadmissible trigonometric values.
Evaluate the original parametric coordinates exactly at the retained angle.
walkthrough:
The tangent is parallel to the $y$-axis when the gradient is vertical, which occurs when $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = 0$ (and $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}\theta} \ne 0$):
$$2\cos\theta + 2\cos 2\theta = 0$$
$$\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta = 0$$

Select the valid solution in the open interval $0 < \theta < \pi$:
- $\cos\theta = -1 \implies \theta = \pi$ (excluded as $\theta < \pi$).
- $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
